Lesson 65

Father · Tom: What are you going to do this evening, Jill?

Jill: I’m going to meet some friends, Dad.

Lesson 65

Father · Tom: What are you going to do this evening, Jill?

Jill: I’m going to meet some friends, Dad.

Father · Tom: You mustn’t come home late. You must be home at half past ten.

Jill: I can’t get home so early, Dad!

Lesson 65

Jill: Can I have the key to the front door, please?

Father · Tom: No, you can’t.

Lesson 65

Jill: Can I have the key to the front door, please?

Father · Tom: No, you can’t.

Mother: Jill’s eighteen years old, Tom. She’s not a baby. Give her the key. She always comes home early.

Lesson 65

Jill: Can I have the key to the front door, please?

Father · Tom: No, you can’t.

Mother: Jill’s eighteen years old, Tom. She’s not a baby. Give her the key. She always comes home early.

Lesson 65

Mother: Jill’s eighteen years old, Tom. She’s not a baby. Give her the key. She always comes home early.

Father · Tom: Oh, all right!

Father · Tom: Here you are. But you mustn’t come home after a quarter past eleven. Do you hear?

Jill: Yes, Dad.

Lesson 65

Father · Tom: What are you going to do this evening, Jill?

Jill: I’m going to meet some friends, Dad.

Jill: Thanks, Mum.

Mother: That’s all right. Goodbye. Enjoy yourself!

Jill: We always enjoy ourselves, Mum. Bye-bye.

Lesson 65

Father · Tom: What are you going to do this evening, Jill?

Jill: I’m going to meet some friends, Dad.

Father · Tom: You mustn’t come home late. You must be home at half past ten.

Jill: I can’t get home so early, Dad!

Jill: Can I have the key to the front door, please?

Father · Tom: No, you can’t.

Mother: Jill’s eighteen years old, Tom. She’s not a baby. Give her the key. She always comes home early.

Father · Tom: Oh, all right!

Father · Tom: Here you are. But you mustn’t come home after a quarter past eleven. Do you hear?

Jill: Yes, Dad.

Jill: Thanks, Mum.

Mother: That’s all right. Goodbye. Enjoy yourself!

Jill: We always enjoy ourselves, Mum. Bye-bye.
